haiku-low.q1: Nothing is signed in. No session row is created. The server creates a five-minute challenge and sets the mfa cookie, then asks for a second-step code.
haiku-low.q2: Only after a valid code confirms the new setup, which makes the pending secret active. Until then sign-in ignores it. During a replacement, the old factor keeps working.
haiku-low.q3: The unused recovery code is consumed atomically and a session is created. Sign-in does not depend on the notification email, which is sent after commit and retried in the background if it fails.
haiku-low.q4: The fifth wrong entry, or a submission after five minutes, ends it. The challenge is deleted, the mfa cookie cleared, and the user returns to the password step.
haiku-low.q5: Every other session of that user is deleted. Only the current session, identified by its cookie hash, stays.
haiku-low.q6: No. Only steps later than last_used_step are accepted, so replays fail. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step either side of the current step.
haiku-low.q7: Pending becomes active, old active secret is removed, last_used_step is recorded, old recovery codes are deleted, 10 new ones inserted, other sessions deleted, all in one transaction. Partial-failure outcome is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Server-side in mfa_challenges as a sha256 hash. The browser holds the raw token in the mfa cookie. Deleted on success, fifth wrong entry, or expiry submission.
haiku-low.q9: Secret and status in totp_secrets, with last_used_step. Recovery codes as hashes in recovery_codes. 2FA is on when an active totp_secrets row exists, since sign-in reads only active rows.
haiku-low.q10: The old active secret keeps protecting sign-in until the replacement is confirmed. If abandoned, 2FA stays on with the old secret.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED how the step distinguishes them. Wrong recovery codes count: used, unknown, and invalid entries all count toward the limit of five.
haiku-low.q12: NOT DESIGNED. The Open state has no exit; product has not decided whether support may reset 2FA or how identity would be checked.

sonnet.q1: A challenge: a random token's sha256 is stored in mfa_challenges (5 min expiry, failed_attempts 0) and an mfa cookie is set. No session row and no sid cookie is created. The mfa cookie grants no access.
sonnet.q2: Only after the user confirms setup with a valid code. Until then the secret is pending and sign-in ignores it. For a replacement, the old active secret keeps working until the new one is confirmed.
sonnet.q3: The matching recovery code is atomically marked used (UPDATE ... SET used_at = now() WHERE used_at IS NULL), the challenge is deleted and start_session creates the session. After commit, enqueue_email is called with the count of unused codes left. Sign-in does not depend on the email. If the send fails it is retried in the background and sign-in is unaffected.
sonnet.q4: The fifth wrong entry, or a submission after expires_at (5 minutes). The challenge row is deleted and the mfa cookie cleared. The user goes back to the password step and must re-enter the password.
sonnet.q5: On confirm, every other session of the user is deleted (WHERE user_id = $1 AND token_hash <> sha256(current cookie)). The current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. Only steps later than last_used_step are accepted, enforced by an atomic update. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step before and one after the current step.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: the pending secret becomes active and any old active secret is removed. last_used_step is recorded. All old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted. All other sessions are deleted. A wrong or already used code changes nothing and issues no codes, and the user can retry. What happens if the transaction itself fails partway is NOT STATED, though it is described as one transaction.
sonnet.q8: Stored on the server in the mfa_challenges table (challenge_hash = sha256 of the token, user_id, expires_at, failed_attempts). The browser refers to it with the mfa cookie holding the raw token (httponly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 5 min max-age). It is removed by deleting the row on success, on the 5th wrong entry or on expiry. The cookie is cleared on discard.
sonnet.q9: The secret is in totp_secrets as secret_sealed (sealed with AES-GCM, key in the KMS), with status (pending or active) and last_used_step. Recovery codes are in recovery_codes (user_id, code_hash, used_at). '2FA on' means the user has an active totp_secrets row, since sign-in reads only active rows. The document does not state this as an explicit definition.
sonnet.q10: The old active secret keeps working, so sign-in is still protected by the old factor. A wrong code on the replacement changes nothing. If the user abandons setup, 2FA stays on with the old secret. Note that starting the replacement does not ask for the old code, and that is an open question.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how it tells them apart. The document says the user submits 'an authenticator code or a recovery code to the challenge endpoint' but does not say how the server distinguishes them. Yes, wrong, used or unknown recovery codes count as one wrong entry toward the limit of five.
sonnet.q12: There is none. It is not designed and the Open state has no way out. Product has not decided whether support may reset 2FA or how identity would be checked.
